parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal passport sex-marker restriction now in force, with confiscations and stranding documented; federal entry screening that refuses discrepant documents and raises lifetime-ineligibility possibility; federal immigration and corrections practices with documented abuse of trans detainees; and, in one division, a private-enforcement bounty law plus licence invalidation and facility bans reaching airports. Four states criminalise trans bathroom use in some circumstances, with a documented arrest. Traveller protections are real but partial: a national hate-crime statute and a national employment ruling, 22 states plus DC with gender-identity discrimination bans, and some federal orders enjoined. The division's hate-crime law omits gender identity and the bounty suit's outcome is unresolved. Universal exposure is documented, with no trans-specific killings recorded. This sits in the High Risk band, above the birth-sex custody and bathroom-arrest tier and below regimes with organised sweeps or capital charging.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passports issued only as M or F by birth/sex-at-birth documents since 2025; X markers ended for new issue; passports confiscated or blocked, leaving some stranded. Entry screening refuses discrepant cases and may pursue permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; litigation pending (civil-liberties suit, seven plaintiffs); no operative traveller-facing remedy documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-country passport mismatch triggers secondary screening, refusal, and fraud-ground risk; airline and airport screening can out the traveller before any state action.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Division trespass arrest documented (handcuffed, 24 hours held in men's ward, charge up to 60 days). Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections adopted birth-sex-based conversion-therapy policies and stopped reporting counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release available in the one documented arrest; no operative custody protection for trans detainees documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility rules place trans detainees by birth-sex or conversion policy; document discrepancy at entry can lead to immigration detention, linking entry to abusive custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal facilities bar gender-identity-congruent use in federally funded single-sex facilities. Facility bans cover government buildings in 19 states/provinces plus one unit, schools in 3, and some private settings in 6. Four criminalise bathroom use in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states/provinces, 4 units and DC have no mapped ban; the map notes other sex-definition laws may still apply.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor's route through a restricted state faces the same facility rules as residents, including airports and government buildings; federal orders, partly enjoined, set the national baseline.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors banned in 27 states/provinces plus division; October 2025 proposed federal rules would bar public reimbursement for under-18s. Federal subpoenas sought full records of under-19 patients. Corrections care denial documented.
care_services.protection: Federal subpoena and rules are unresolved or enjoined; no traveller care-access protection documented.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking minors or their guardians can become investigated subjects, linking medical access to federal enforcement and records disclosure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders frame gender-affirming care as mutilation, direct law enforcement at schools promoting 'gender ideology', and recast 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a counterterrorism priority. Division law makes wrong-sex facility use a crime with private bounty suits.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism statement disclaims targeting people who disagree; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing plus private bounty enforcement means discovery can come from any member of the public, with no state actor required.

minors_guardians.exposure: A minor's passport and school records follow birth sex; school staff using preferred names face potential prosecution; minors' care is banned or subpoenaed. A guardian travelling with a minor faces facility rules and parental exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: Teacher-injunction and some school protections exist in limited, dated form; no operative minor-specific shield for travelling families documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Document mismatch for a minor at entry or in hospital can expose both the minor and the guardian to investigation and separation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific killing rate documented. Bounty-law suits enable private harassment of visibly trans people in public buildings. National bias statute covers gender-identity hate crimes but only 23 states/provinces cover them; 37 lacked anti-bias statutes as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and national employment ruling apply; 22 states plus DC ban gender-identity discrimination; division anti-discrimination law covers employment, housing and public accommodation since 2020.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Patchy state coverage means visitors' recourse depends on route; federal protections exist but are not reliably enforced against private bounty suits.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division bounty-law lawsuit unresolved; invalidation notices and bounty-suit counts unrecorded; federal passport suit pending; enforcement data for facility provisions not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties and legal-aid organisations provide FAQs and litigation; several federal orders enjoined; courts have issued some restraining orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outcomes of pending suits determine whether current exposure persists; visitors cannot predict which measures will apply at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: birth-sex custody with documented assaults, cross-dressing arrests in administrative buildings, and slow remedies. This dossier is similar on custody and facility exposure, and adds documented passport stranding and private bounty suits. It is lower in severity because it has no capital provisions, no documented sweeps, and a national hate-crime statute. It sits at or slightly below 0.25-C.

0.35-A has universal entry refusal and departure forced without arrest, with appeals almost never granted. This dossier has refusal for discrepant documents and possible lifetime ineligibility, plus documented custody abuse, which is more severe. Protections such as courts operating and pending litigation are somewhat stronger, so it sits near 0.35-A but slightly lower.

0.45-D has universal registration and database exposure with confidential, slow ombuds review and no imprisonment. This dossier has a comparable universal facility exposure and an unresolved ombuds-like process, but adds documented immigration custody abuse and birth-sex custody. It is therefore lower than 0.45-D.

parsed.synthesis: Universal exposures (passport marker mismatch, facility bans in most restricted states, and private bounty enforcement reaching airports) apply to every visitor who routes through restricted jurisdictions. These compound with documented custody harms, including birth-sex placement, forced labour and sexual abuse in immigration detention, and federal conversion-policy in corrections. Partial protections (national hate-crime and employment law, 22 state/province anti-discrimination bans, enjoined orders) do not offset documented traveller-facing exposure, and most outcomes remain pending litigation. The combined regime therefore sits in the High Risk band.
